author.name: Nikita Khrushchev
author.heading: About Nikita Khrushchev
author.bio: Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet Communist Party from 1953 to 1964 and served as Soviet premier from 1958. His leadership combined the denunciation of Stalin’s abuses with Cold War confrontations, including the Cuban Missile Crisis.

cite.sourceCitation: “The living will envy the dead,” attributed to Khrushchev; verification failure reported by Respectfully Quoted (1989), as documented by Wikiquote. Earlier parallels checked in Stevenson’s Treasure Island, chapter XX, and Jeremiah 8:3 (KJV).

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying compresses the fear that survival after catastrophe might be worse than death. That idea long predates the nuclear age: the inspected biblical and adventure-fiction passages express related comparisons in different circumstances and words.

A Cold War name makes the warning seem like an authoritative nuclear threat, but no dated Khrushchev source is established here. Neither a thematic ancestor nor a reported similar sentence by Herman Kahn resolves authorship of the exact popular wording.
